_comment: Ops alerts as code (#201). The api applies these to the 'Overwatch Ops' Grafana org at startup (_provision_ops_alerts). Only the variable parts live here — the contact point, the root notification policy and each rule's SQL/summary. The mechanical reduce->threshold(>0) pipeline, the folder and the per-env `env` label + '[env]' summary prefix are assembled in main.py so the same file serves sandbox/staging/prod. addresses come from OPS_ALERT_EMAIL (.env). See #172/#185/#187 for how this evolved. Freshness rules (#303) use HAVING so a healthy system returns NO ROWS: the threshold is >0, and noDataState is OK, so silence means fresh. Each returns text columns alongside `value`, which Grafana turns into labels, so the e-mail says HOW stale rather than merely that something is. Adding a fourth freshness check is mechanical — copy one, change the table, the column and the interval. Freshness rules must return no column that changes while the condition holds: labels are identity, and a moving label defeats every repeat interval (#341).

rules.title: New user registration
rules._sql_comment: One row per new user -> Grafana turns the text columns into alert labels, so the e-mail names who signed up, their org and country (#185). value=1 keeps the reduce/threshold (>0) firing per user.
rules.sql: SELECT ru.email, ru.name, COALESCE((SELECT string_agg(o.name, ', ') FROM org_user ou JOIN organization o ON o.id = ou.org WHERE ou.sub = ru.sub), '(no org)') AS org, COALESCE(ru.country, '??') AS country, 1 AS value FROM registered_user ru WHERE ru.first_seen > now() - interval '15 minutes' AND ru.email NOT LIKE 'e2e-bot%'

rules.title: New API key requested
rules.sql: SELECT count(*) AS value FROM api_key WHERE created_at > now() - interval '15 minutes'

rules.title: Telemetry ingestion has stalled
rules._sql_comment: The 2026-08-20 outage: ingestion stopped and every other check stayed green for four days. In aggregate the fleet is heard several times an hour, so a 90-minute gap is already abnormal. HAVING returns no row while fresh. Returns only `newest`: a column whose value changes while the condition holds (an age) becomes part of the alert's LABEL set, so every evaluation is a NEW instance and notifies immediately — that is how this mailed hourly forever (#341).
rules.sql: SELECT 1 AS value, COALESCE(to_char(max(ts) AT TIME ZONE 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI'), 'never') AS newest FROM telemetry HAVING max(ts) IS NULL OR max(ts) < now() - interval '90 minutes'
rules.summary: No telemetry stored since {{ $labels.newest }} UTC. The control room is up but blind.

rules.title: Position propagation has stalled
rules._sql_comment: Positions are computed locally by SGP4 from cached elements and depend on NOTHING external, so a gap here means the ingest itself is wedged rather than a provider being unreachable. #230 made propagate_positions dead code and the globe stopped entirely, unnoticed. Returns only `newest`: a column whose value changes while the condition holds (an age) becomes part of the alert's LABEL set, so every evaluation is a NEW instance and notifies immediately — that is how this mailed hourly forever (#341).
rules.sql: SELECT 1 AS value, COALESCE(to_char(max(ts) AT TIME ZONE 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI'), 'never') AS newest FROM position HAVING max(ts) IS NULL OR max(ts) < now() - interval '5 minutes'
rules.summary: No positions propagated since {{ $labels.newest }} UTC. This is local SGP4 — the ingest is wedged, not a provider.

rules.title: Orbital elements are stale
rules._sql_comment: Invisible by construction without an alert: positions keep being produced from old TLEs and drift quietly, so the globe looks alive while it is increasingly wrong. Epoch, not fetched_at — re-fetching the same old element set is not freshness. Returns only `newest`: a column whose value changes while the condition holds (an age) becomes part of the alert's LABEL set, so every evaluation is a NEW instance and notifies immediately — that is how this mailed hourly forever (#341).
rules.sql: SELECT 1 AS value, COALESCE(to_char(max(epoch) AT TIME ZONE 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI'), 'never') AS newest FROM elements HAVING max(epoch) IS NULL OR max(epoch) < now() - interval '24 hours'
rules.summary: Newest orbital element set is from {{ $labels.newest }} UTC. Positions are still being drawn, and drifting.
